source: Tax Foundation, State Individual Income Tax Rates and Brackets, 2026 (state revenue departments). States flagged approximate model a simplified schedule; see notes.

AK.name: Alaska
AK.notes: No tax on wages or retirement income.

AL.name: Alabama
AL.notes: Standard deduction and personal exemption combined; Alabama's income-based deduction phase-down is not modelled.

AR.name: Arkansas
AR.notes: Top rate is 3.7% (H.B. 1001, retroactive to Jan 1, 2026). Bracket widths use 2025 amounts; the Department of Finance's 2026 widths are not confirmed here. Arkansas excludes up to $6,000 of pension and retirement income per person. The cap is counted for every adult of that age, which may overstate it when one spouse has all the retirement income.

CO.name: Colorado
CO.notes: Colorado subtracts up to $20,000 of Social Security per person aged 55 to 64 and $24,000 at 65 or more. Thresholds are from secondary sources and not yet checked against the official form.

CT.name: Connecticut
CT.notes: Connecticut follows the CT-1040 Tax Calculation Schedule (Tables A to E: personal exemption, 2% add-back, recapture and personal tax credit by CT AGI) as printed in the 2024 form (CT-1040 TCS Rev. 12/24); the thresholds are set in law and are not indexed, and no 2026 schedule is published yet. Assumed: the personal tax credit is 100% at or below the first row of Table E. Check against the 2026 form when it appears. Connecticut leaves Social Security out when AGI is at or below $75,000 (single) / $100,000 (joint); above that the federally taxable amount is used (the state caps it at 25% of benefits, so this errs high). Thresholds are from secondary sources and not yet checked against the official form.

DE.name: Delaware
DE.notes: Personal credit $110 per filer. Delaware excludes up to $12,500 of pension and retirement income per person aged 60 or more. The cap is counted for every adult of that age, which may overstate it when one spouse has all the retirement income.

FL.name: Florida
FL.notes: No tax on wages or retirement income.

GA.name: Georgia
GA.notes: Georgia excludes up to $35,000 of retirement income per person aged 62 to 64 and $65,000 at 65 or more. The cap is counted for every adult of that age, which may overstate it when one spouse has all the retirement income.

HI.name: Hawaii
HI.notes: Standard deduction plus personal exemption combined.

IA.name: Iowa
IA.notes: Iowa exempts retirement income for anyone 55 or older (2023 law).

IL.name: Illinois
IL.notes: Illinois exempts retirement income from qualified plans, IRAs and pensions entirely (35 ILCS 5/203(a)(2)(F)).

KS.name: Kansas
KS.notes: Standard deduction plus personal exemption combined.

KY.name: Kentucky
KY.notes: Kentucky excludes up to $31,110 of pension and retirement account income per person. The cap is counted for every adult of that age, which may overstate it when one spouse has all the retirement income.

LA.name: Louisiana
LA.notes: Louisiana exempts up to $12,000 of pension, annuity and IRA distributions for each person 65 or older (IT-540 instructions, code 06E). Federal, state and teacher retirement benefits are fully exempt in Louisiana but are not separated out here.

MA.name: Massachusetts
MA.notes: 5% plus 4% surtax over $1M; personal exemption not modeled.

MD.name: Maryland
MD.notes: Standard deduction and rate schedule match the Comptroller Tax Alert on the 2025 legislative session (rev. Dec 22, 2025): flat $3,350 single / $6,700 joint plus the $3,200 exemption per person, with new 6.25% and 6.5% top brackets. Not modelled: exemption phase-out at higher incomes; county income tax is not included.

ME.name: Maine
ME.notes: Standard deduction plus personal exemption; high-income phase-outs not modelled.

MN.name: Minnesota
MN.notes: Standard deduction phase-out at higher incomes is not modelled. Minnesota's Social Security subtraction is full below $84,490 (single) / $108,320 (joint) AGI and phases out above; here it is all or nothing. Thresholds are from secondary sources and not yet checked against the official form.

MO.name: Missouri
MO.notes: Same schedule for all filers; follows the federal standard deduction.

MS.name: Mississippi
MS.notes: Mississippi exempts qualified retirement income (pensions, IRA and 401(k) withdrawals) once the owner is 59 and a half or retired; modelled from age 60.

MT.name: Montana
MT.notes: Follows the federal standard deduction. Montana deducts $5,500 (single) / $11,000 (joint) of taxable Social Security. Thresholds are from secondary sources and not yet checked against the official form.

NH.name: New Hampshire
NH.notes: No tax on wages or retirement income.

NJ.name: New Jersey
NJ.notes: Personal exemption only; no standard deduction. Pension exclusion (nj.gov Retirement Income Exclusions, 2025): age 62 or older, pension, annuity and IRA withdrawals up to $75,000 single / $100,000 joint / $50,000 separate when total income is $100,000 or less, then 37.5/18.75% (single), 50/25% (joint) of them up to $125,000 / $150,000, none above. Total income here is AGI less taxable Social Security. The separate Other Retirement Income Exclusion is not modelled.

NM.name: New Mexico
NM.notes: Follows the federal standard deduction. New Mexico leaves Social Security out when AGI is at or below $100,000 (single) / $150,000 (joint). Thresholds are from secondary sources and not yet checked against the official form.

NV.name: Nevada
NV.notes: No tax on wages or retirement income.

NY.name: New York
NY.notes: Includes the benefit recapture for AGI over $107,650 (IT-201-I 2025 tax computation worksheets). Rates are the 2026 schedule; recapture amounts are derived from them. NYC and Yonkers taxes are not included. New York excludes up to $20,000 of pension and annuity income per person aged 59 and a half or more (modelled from 60). The cap is counted for every adult of that age, which may overstate it when one spouse has all the retirement income.

OK.name: Oklahoma
OK.notes: Standard deduction plus personal exemption combined. Oklahoma excludes up to $10,000 of pension and retirement income per person. The cap is counted for every adult of that age, which may overstate it when one spouse has all the retirement income.

OR.name: Oregon
OR.notes: Personal exemption credit $256 per filer; the federal-tax subtraction is not modelled.

PA.name: Pennsylvania
PA.notes: Pennsylvania does not tax retirement income (pensions, IRA and 401(k) withdrawals) once the owner has reached retirement age; modelled from age 60.

RI.name: Rhode Island
RI.notes: Standard deduction plus personal exemption; high-income phase-outs not modelled. Rhode Island leaves Social Security out for people at full retirement age with AGI at or below $107,000 (single) / $133,750 (joint). Thresholds are from secondary sources and not yet checked against the official form.

SC.name: South Carolina
SC.notes: Same schedule for all filers. South Carolina deducts up to $10,000 of retirement income per person aged 65 or more. The cap is counted for every adult of that age, which may overstate it when one spouse has all the retirement income.

SD.name: South Dakota
SD.notes: No tax on wages or retirement income.

TN.name: Tennessee
TN.notes: No tax on wages or retirement income.

TX.name: Texas
TX.notes: No tax on wages or retirement income.

UT.name: Utah
UT.notes: Utah gives a credit that fully offsets tax on Social Security below $54,000 (single) / $90,000 (joint) AGI and phases out above; here it is all or nothing. Thresholds are from secondary sources and not yet checked against the official form.

VA.name: Virginia
VA.notes: Virginia's age deduction is $12,000 for each person 65 or older, reduced $1 for every $1 that income (AGI less taxable Social Security) is over $50,000 single / $75,000 married (tax.virginia.gov/subtractions). The older rule for people born before 1939 is not modelled.

VT.name: Vermont
VT.notes: Brackets and standard deduction + exemption from the 2025 IN-111 instructions (2026 widths unpublished). Over $150,000 AGI, tax is at least 3% of AGI (the US-interest subtraction is not modelled). Vermont leaves Social Security out when AGI is at or below $55,000 (single) / $70,000 (joint), and phases it in above that; the full amount is used here. Thresholds are from secondary sources and not yet checked against the official form.

WA.name: Washington
WA.notes: No tax on wages or retirement income.

WI.name: Wisconsin
WI.notes: Sliding-scale standard deduction is shown at its maximum. From 2025 each person 67 or older may subtract up to $24,000 of retirement income (Publication 126, 1/26); the smaller $5,000 subtraction at 65 for incomes under $15,000 / $30,000 is not modelled. Claiming the subtraction forgoes Wisconsin tax credits, which are not modelled.

WV.name: West Virginia
WV.notes: Personal exemption only; no standard deduction.

WY.name: Wyoming
WY.notes: No tax on wages or retirement income.
